title: A Warmer Slot for the Panel
story: The department listed oral slots alphabetically, leaving Malik last after a wait that dulled his examples. He asked to join the students who shared his case, so the context stayed warm for the panel. Professor Shah agreed, provided Malik heard none of the earlier answers. He waited outside and entered with that cluster. Feedback noted sharper comparisons than his previous solo slot.

vocabulary.definition: In the order of the letters of the names
The surrounding information needed to understand something
The group of examiners hearing the talks
Judgments about how things differ or match

quiz.question: Why did Malik’s oral slot fall at the end?
options: The slots were listed in alphabetical order
He had asked to hear every earlier answer
The panel wanted a colder context
His solo slot had already been judged sharper
quiz.correctAnswer: The slots were listed in alphabetical order
quiz.explanation: The department listed the slots alphabetically, and that left him last.
quiz.supportingSentence: The department listed oral slots alphabetically, leaving Malik last after a wait that dulled his examples.

quiz.question: What condition did Professor Shah attach to the move?
options: Malik must not hear the answers given before his
He had to present without a case at all
The panel would mark only the wait outside
Comparisons had to be shorter than before
quiz.correctAnswer: Malik must not hear the answers given before his
quiz.explanation: Shah agreed only if Malik heard none of the earlier answers.
quiz.supportingSentence: Professor Shah agreed, provided Malik heard none of the earlier answers.

quiz.question: What does the sharper feedback suggest about the grouping?
options: The panel could compare work while the shared case was still fresh
Alphabetical order always produces higher marks
Waiting outside removed the need for examples
Solo slots are marked more kindly than groups
quiz.correctAnswer: The panel could compare work while the shared case was still fresh
quiz.explanation: Sharper comparisons than his solo slot fit the aim of keeping the shared case warm for the panel.
quiz.supportingSentence: Feedback noted sharper comparisons than his previous solo slot.

quiz.question: What does cluster mean in this passage?
options: The group of students who shared his case
A long wait in alphabetical order
The corridor outside the exam room
A mark given for a solo slot
quiz.correctAnswer: The group of students who shared his case
quiz.explanation: He entered with that cluster, the students he had asked to join.
quiz.supportingSentence: He waited outside and entered with that cluster.

quiz.question: Why does the writer mention the dulled examples?
options: To show the harm of waiting until the very end
To prove the panel disliked his case
To suggest alphabetical lists are forbidden
To argue that corridors should be silent
quiz.correctAnswer: To show the harm of waiting until the very end
quiz.explanation: The dull examples explain why being last was a problem worth fixing.
quiz.supportingSentence: The department listed oral slots alphabetically, leaving Malik last after a wait that dulled his examples.
